drafts.title: Voice assistant understands common driving commands reliably
drafts.description: When driving, the voice assistant recognizes and executes common, simple driver commands (navigation destinations, climate intents, media control, phone calls) without repeating or requiring multiple attempts.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a standardized test with in-cabin background noise up to 70 dB(A), the system correctly understands and executes at least 95% of a 100-item set of common driving commands within 3 seconds.
assumptions: Test uses a representative 100-command list derived from logged customer requests and dealer scripts.
Cloud assistance may be allowed for initial deployment; offline fallback assumed for occasional loss of connectivity.
uncertainties: Performance may vary with non-native accents and rare commands not in the test set.
Ambient cabin noise levels in extreme conditions (>70 dB(A)) may reduce recognition rates.

drafts.title: Wireless charging works reliably for compatible phones
drafts.description: When a compatible phone is placed on the vehicle wireless charging pad as instructed, it continuously charges without unexpected dropouts or repeated re-centering prompts.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Across a representative set of three major phone form factors, at least 95% of charging sessions maintain continuous charging for a two-hour continuous drive test with no interruption reported by the phone and no driver intervention.
assumptions: Phones tested are Qi-compatible and have up-to-date firmware.
Charging pad is used as instructed (phone placed centrally, no heavy cases unless specified).
uncertainties: Third-party phone cases, metal attachments, or damaged phone coils may still cause failures.
Wireless charging behavior can vary across phone OS updates.

drafts.title: Head-up display and center screen remain readable in bright sunlight
drafts.description: Drivers can read critical HUD information and primary center-screen content quickly even under direct bright sunlight and common sun angles.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a usability test with 20 participants under direct sunlight conditions (ambient illuminance ≥80,000 lux / typical bright sun), at least 90% of participants can correctly read the HUD speed readout and identify main center-screen icons within 2 seconds.
assumptions: Test uses standardized bright-sunlight test rig and representative screen/HUD brightness settings.
Participants represent a range of driver heights and eyeglass/no-eyeglass conditions.
uncertainties: Extreme glare from aftermarket windshield films or damaged windshields may still reduce legibility.
Perception varies with driver eyesight; accessibility adjustments may be required.

drafts.title: Tactile physical controls for temperature and fan speed operable without looking
drafts.description: Drivers can change cabin temperature and fan speed by feel using tactile physical controls, without needing to look at the controls or screen.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a blind-touch usability test with 20 participants, at least 90% can change cabin temperature by ±2°C and increase or decrease fan speed by one level within 2 seconds solely by touch.
assumptions: Controls are ergonomically placed within the driver's natural reach zone.
Tactile differences (shape/texture) are used to distinguish temperature vs. fan controls.
uncertainties: Drivers with reduced tactile sensitivity or wearing thick gloves may have reduced success rates.
Integration with heater/AC modes may require clear tactile affordances.

drafts.title: Heated steering wheel included in the cold-weather package
drafts.description: When customers select the vehicle cold-weather package, the heated steering wheel is included as part of that package rather than offered only as a separate costly standalone option.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: For all configurations where the cold-weather (winter) package is selected, the heated steering wheel is included 100% of the time in the package contents.
assumptions: Package contents are consistent across trims in the target market at launch.
Market-specific regulatory or supplier constraints do not prevent inclusion.
uncertainties: Regional variations in supplier availability could necessitate temporary exceptions.
Dealer-level bundling practices may vary unless centrally enforced.

drafts.title: Driver profile: view, export and delete personal data from the vehicle
drafts.description: Drivers can manage personal profile data directly in the vehicle: view what data is stored, export a copy, and permanently delete their profile and associated personal data without requiring a dealer visit.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: From the driver profile UI, a user can (1) view a list of stored personal data types, (2) export an archived copy to a connected device within 5 minutes, and (3) permanently delete the profile so that vehicle-local personal data is removed within 24 hours; the UI shows a clear confirmation and a timestamp of completion.
assumptions: Cloud-stored profile data deletion may require up to 24 hours to propagate and may depend on backend APIs and connectivity.
Export requires a connected device (USB or paired phone) and sufficient free space.
uncertainties: Deletion semantics for anonymized telemetry vs. identifiable profile data may require legal definitions.
Some OEM cloud backups or third-party services may retain copies beyond vehicle-local deletion.

drafts.title: Request for China CCC certification (out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the infotainment system passes CCC certification for the Chinese market.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This item is a regulatory certification request and is out of scope for product feature requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/certification request (homologation) — implementation is governed by compliance process, not a customer-facing product requirement.

drafts.title: Request for specific cockpit chip (Snapdragon 8295) (out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers requested that the cockpit computer uses the Snapdragon 8295 chip.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a request for a specific engineering component and is out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering specification — requests for specific chips/components are handled in engineering requirements, not as customer-facing outcomes.

drafts.title: Requests related to base price, lease, subscriptions and discounts (out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers requested lower base price, cheaper lease, free packages, package discounts, lower dealer margin, subscription prices, financing offers, or complained about option pricing.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: These items concern pricing, financing and dealer margin and are out of scope for product feature requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Pricing, financing and dealer margin requests — business/price topics are out of scope for vehicle feature requirements.
